why_explainers.question: Why does India need its own GPS?
why_explainers.answer: During the **1999 Kargil conflict**, India couldn't rely on foreign navigation data. Our own system means **no one can switch it off** for us.

why_explainers.question: Why do you need four satellites?
why_explainers.answer: Your phone works out position from **distances to satellites**. Three fix the spot; a **fourth corrects the clock**, giving accurate 3D position.

why_explainers.question: Why carry atomic clocks?
why_explainers.answer: Navigation depends on **super-precise timing**. NVS-03 carries **Indian-made rubidium atomic clocks**, accurate to billionths of a second.

**NVS-01**, the first second-generation NavIC satellite, was launched.
**NVS-03** is slated to launch from Sriharikota on 30 October.

stories.title: India plans four rocket launch pads by 2029
stories.teaser: More launch pads mean more rockets, and more chances to explore space.

Std 7–8.headline: India plans four rocket launch pads by 2029
in_3_lines: ISRO, India's space agency, says India will have **four working rocket launch pads** by 2029.
Today India launches its big rockets from **two pads at Sriharikota** in Andhra Pradesh.
More pads mean ISRO can **launch more often**: more satellites, Moon missions and astronauts.

why_explainers.question: Why does India need more launch pads?
why_explainers.answer: A rocket sits on its pad for **weeks** before launch. More pads let ISRO prepare **several rockets at once**, like adding computers to a busy school lab.

why_explainers.question: Why build a new launch site in Tamil Nadu?
why_explainers.answer: Rockets heading south from Sriharikota must **curve around Sri Lanka**, which wastes fuel. **Kulasekarapattinam** in Tamil Nadu lets small rockets fly straight south over the sea.

why_explainers.question: Why launch rockets over the sea?
why_explainers.answer: If something goes wrong, falling rocket parts land in the **empty sea**, not on homes. That is why launch sites like Sriharikota sit on the **coast**.

backstory.point: India launched its **first rocket** from Thumba in Kerala. Parts were famously carried on a **bicycle**!
**Chandrayaan-3** landed near the Moon's south pole after launching from Sriharikota.
ISRO's chief says **four launch pads** will be ready by 2029.

**Private Indian companies** are now building rockets too, and they also need places to launch from.

why_explainers.answer: It is an **apex predator**, at the top of the food chain. It keeps animals like **wild goats** in balance, so grass and slopes stay healthy.
